title: Physics-Informed Spatial Ensemble Machine Learning: Smart Water Leakage Detection and Spatial Localization
content: Non-revenue water from undetected leaks remains a persistent inefficiency of urban infrastructure, and benchmark datasets showcasing machine-learning (ML) leak-detection pipelines are reused as baselines without independent scrutiny. This study audited a widely circulated smart-water leak-detection dataset (n = 5000 IoT-simulated readings; 125 georeferenced Zone-Block-Pipe segments) and found its binary leak label to be an exact function of two of its own predictors, rendering standard random-split evaluations circular. A physics-informed, spatially explicit classifier is proposed instead: hydraulically interpretable resistance, fatigue and zonal-anomaly indices replace the raw threshold-preserving ratios, validated under Leave-One-Zone-Out spatial cross-validation, after which Getis-Ord Gi* statistics localize candidate leak clusters. The classifier attained 99.40% accuracy, F1 = 0.9531 and MCC = 0.9500 (ROC-AUC = 0.9985); decision-level fusion with an Isolation Forest anomaly channel did not improve on this result, a negative, significance-tested finding. Global Moran's I on the risk score (I = −0.0002, p = 0.53) confirmed complete spatial randomness, and the Gi* hotspot rate matched the nominal Type-I error; a neighbour-only spatial-lag check traced the residual Gi*-leak association to a self-inclusion artefact rather than genuine contagion. The framework offers an interpretable, leakage-free, spatially aware alternative to circular threshold-recovery pipelines, giving utilities a calibrated basis for prioritizing field inspection.
